_: Text of the README 'How it works' figure (v2/where-chock-sits.png), read by where-chock-sits.mjs. The figure is a session as an ordered path with checkpoints. 'points' are the 12 agentseam events (agentseam.contract.EVENTS) plus the five other places Chock acts or could: 'place' says where each is drawn (a diamond on the arrow into a path step, the MCP tag, or a chip in the More hooks row); 'acts' is true where shipped Chock code acts on the point (filled); 'does' is the at-most-four-word note under a filled diamond. tests/test_readme_picture.py asserts the agentseam points equal agentseam.contract.EVENTS, the acting set equals what the engine handles, and (with node) that no two shapes of the layout intersect. 'proof' lists the tests that prove each acting point.
title: A session, step by step. Chock runs at the marked points.
footer: The rules are files in your repository. A person turns them on once with chock sync.
alt: A session as an ordered path with checkpoints. Inside your agent: you open a session, type a request, the agent loads its rules, the model picks the next action, a tool runs (repeating until done) and the agent ends its turn; then in your repository: git commit, git push, CI on the pull request and the main branch. Diamonds on the arrows are the hook points: filled where Chock runs today (session start, rules, before and after a tool, stop, the MCP gateway, commit, push, CI) and hollow where a policy of your own can run; the other agent events sit in a row of more hooks.
